paper_metadata.title: Optimizing strength through tailored lamellar heterogeneous structures in Mg-5Y-1Sn alloys using gradient extrusion

evidence.quote: Nominal composition of the tested alloy is Mg-5Y-1Sn, utilizing commercially pure Mg (99.9 wt%), an Mg-Y (30 wt%) intermediate alloy, and high-purity Sn (99.99 wt%) as its actual ingredients.

In an electric furnace at roughly 720 ◦ C, the material is entirely melted with a combination of protective gases (SF6: CO2 = 1: 99) to avoid oxidation, then it is transferred into a hot steel mold and allowed to air-cool, producing cylindrical ingots 90 mm in diameter.
Afterward, the ingot is heated to 500 ◦ C for 24 h and then allowed to cool in the air to achieve homogenization.
